content.comment_body: I created a small program (one page) which previously worked, but after making changes, I can't start simulation mode. The system says there are unconnected contacts. If I let it auto-connect them, I get a java null pointer exception and simulation fails. If I don't let it auto-connect, the simulation won't enter 'run' mode. I tried moving each element to check for hidden issues, deleted and reconnected everything, but it still fails. Is there a way for [product_name] to specifically show me where the missing connections are?
You can use the F2 key. Then you'll see options available in [product_name], along with a summary of errors and so on.

Hello, do you program in LAD? If so, try switching to FBD and then correct the issue. This is a known limitation of LAD—when copying and pasting, ensure: 1) Don't copy/paste the connection to the left 'power line.' 2) If you want to copy FBs, select the FB-Bit as well before pasting. 3) Or simply switch temporarily to FBD. Hope this helps.

Thanks for the suggestion. I tried pressing F2 and it shows 'Open Connectors: 0/16,' so I'm still unsure what the problem is. The program compiles without errors, but the simulator still reports open connectors.

I'll check this immediately. I've moved several objects and will try deleting every connection to the left bus, then recreating them. I just did that, but it didn't solve the issue. Since the program is small, I think I'll rewrite it from scratch. This feels like it might be a bug in [product_name].
If you share your program here, we can review it and help you troubleshoot.

I reentered the same program and it now runs flawlessly in the simulator. I suspect there was a bug. Previously, when editing and adding connections, I noticed the line didn't always track from the source to the mouse—only appearing when clicking the target contact. In future, if I experience this again, I'll revert to a backup. Thanks for offering to help; it seems the program logic was fine, but another issue caused the problem.

If you still have the old version of your program that fails to run, consider posting it here. We can help figure out what went wrong. This is common in LAD programming, especially after moving contacts; connectors may look connected but actually aren't.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced difficulties troubleshooting unconnected-contact errors in [product_name], where the error messages did not match what was visible in the editor. Attempts to resolve included deleting and remaking connections and using built-in error tools, but the simulator continued to report issues. Rewriting the program cleared the problem, indicating a likely software bug impacting program editing and simulation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the software to accurately indicate where open or unconnected contacts exist in logic diagrams, and to offer effective debugging or error reporting tools for quick resolution.
